company_name: Miro Consulting (website currently presents the business primarily as ECCO Select; the relationship or rebranding status is not explained in the supplied evidence)
value_proposition: Provides software asset and license management services intended to reduce software and cloud costs, maintain license compliance, improve contract and support decisions, and reduce audit exposure. The company markets a performance guarantee under which identified cost savings will exceed its fees.
target_customers: Large enterprises with complex Oracle, Microsoft, IBM, Adobe, Salesforce, AWS, or other cloud/software estates
Organizations facing or preparing for software-license audits
Organizations seeking ongoing outsourced software asset management
IT, procurement, finance, and software-asset-management stakeholders responsible for licensing, subscriptions, support renewals, and cloud costs
Multinational organizations with on-premises and cloud deployments
products_services: Software-vendor negotiation tactics and purchasing guidance
Cloud-cost and environment optimization, demonstrated through AWS customer case studies
Oracle license resale or purchase facilitation, demonstrated in a customer case study
Adobe services are referenced in the service description and navigation, but no specific Adobe offerings are detailed in the supplied evidence
core_technology: Proprietary tools claimed by the company, with no architecture or functionality disclosed
Analyst-led review of software deployments, entitlements, usage, contracts, and purchasing documents
Continuous license-position tracking within managed services
Cost comparison analysis between perpetual licenses and cloud subscriptions
Quarterly Business Reviews for planned infrastructure and licensing changes
Licensing Help Desk for policy, version, and compliance questions
use_cases: Establishing and continuously maintaining an effective license position
Preparing for and responding to Oracle, Microsoft, or IBM audits
Finding errors, omissions, and incorrect calculations in vendor or auditor findings
Reducing audit settlements and financial exposure
Optimizing software-license purchases and deployment configurations
Identifying unused licenses and reducing shelfware
Evaluating perpetual-license costs against cloud-subscription costs
Planning hardware, cloud, and software changes without creating licensing shortfalls
Negotiating enterprise agreements, ULA terms, discounts, and cloud-use rights
Optimizing AWS spending and cloud environments
industries_served: Other large enterprises; the website describes several customers only by size or organization type
business_model: Professional consulting and advisory fees, long-term managed-services engagements described as subscriptions, and Oracle reseller activity demonstrated in one case study. Exact revenue mix and commercial terms are not disclosed.
deployment_model: Remote assistance through phone, email, webchat, and scheduled meetings
Assessment of customer on-premises, cloud, and hybrid software environments; no deployable software product or hosting model is described
enterprise_features: Continuous monitoring of licensing, deployments, entitlements, usage, contracts, and purchasing records
Planning support for infrastructure and cloud changes
Performance guarantee stating that uncovered savings will exceed fees
major_customers: Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative (SMECO), identified by name in an AWS optimization case study
United States Army, identified by name in a case study claiming savings above $60 million
Large federal agency, unnamed; case study claims audit findings were reduced by 97% and $243 million
Multinational health organization, unnamed; case study claims $20 million in savings
Global pharmaceutical company, unnamed; case study claims more than $18 million in savings
Multinational manufacturing organization, unnamed; case study claims more than $5 million in licensing savings
Large public utility, identified elsewhere in the evidence as SMECO
Large publisher, unnamed; case study claims $800,000 in savings
geographic_presence: Global provider status is claimed by the company, but no office footprint or country-by-country coverage is disclosed
United States customer activity is demonstrated through SMECO, the United States Army, and a federal-agency case study
Multinational customer engagements are described, but specific service-delivery locations are not provided
strengths: Broad coverage of major enterprise software vendors, including Oracle, Microsoft, IBM, Salesforce, and references to Adobe
Combination of one-time reviews, audit defense, negotiation support, and continuous managed services
Multiple case studies report substantial cost savings and audit-exposure reductions
Proactive positioning emphasizes compliance assessment before an audit rather than only reacting afterward
Performance guarantee lowers perceived financial risk by promising that identified savings will exceed fees
Case-study evidence demonstrates ongoing operational practices such as continuous license tracking, Quarterly Business Reviews, renewal tracking, and a help desk
Partnerships span major software vendors, AWS, distributors, and managed infrastructure providers
Demonstrated ability to address both on-premises and cloud licensing questions
weaknesses: The supplied website alternates between Miro Consulting and ECCO Select without explaining the corporate, acquisition, or rebranding relationship, creating identity confusion
Most showcased customers are anonymized, limiting independent validation and referenceability
The company calls its tools proprietary but supplies no technical detail, product demonstrations, interfaces, or implementation information
Detailed service coverage is uneven: Oracle offerings are extensive, while Adobe and Salesforce coverage is less fully described
No public pricing, service tiers, engagement duration, or standard scope is disclosed
Many competitive and leadership statements, including 'only' and 'leading,' are marketing claims without comparative evidence
The site presents savings outcomes but does not disclose baseline methodology, sample size, time frame, or whether results are typical
No customer portal, automation, security, integration, or data-governance capabilities are documented
competitive_differentiators: A performance guarantee stating that uncovered cost savings will exceed the company's fees
Proactive compliance reviews before audits rather than exclusively reactive audit defense
Claimed access through the Oracle Partner Program to special pricing, terms, conditions, and support options
Claimed independence combined with demonstrated Oracle reseller activity
Claim of having founded the software-licensing consulting industry more than 20 years ago; not independently substantiated by the supplied evidence
Claimed proprietary tools and a long-tenured team of expert analysts
Continuous managed-service model covering licensing, deployments, entitlements, usage, contracts, and purchasing records
Case-study evidence of challenging audit calculations and negotiating cloud and ULA usage rights
customer_problems_addressed: Unexpected financial exposure from software-license noncompliance
Complex and changing software-vendor licensing rules and policies
Poor visibility into deployments, entitlements, usage, and available licenses
Difficulty negotiating vendor contracts, enterprise agreements, subscriptions, and audit settlements
Licensing risks created by hardware upgrades, software upgrades, virtualization, and cloud migration
Time consumed by internal teams gathering audit data
Fragmented license purchasing and enterprise agreements
Uncertainty when comparing perpetual licensing with cloud subscriptions
technical_risks: The website does not explain how proprietary tools collect, normalize, reconcile, or secure customer deployment and entitlement data
Service outcomes may depend on the completeness and accuracy of customer inventories, contracts, purchasing records, and usage data
Changing vendor policies, product-use rights, and cloud rules can make compliance conclusions time-sensitive
No disclosed integrations with discovery, configuration-management, procurement, cloud-billing, or IT asset-management systems
No information is provided about security certifications, access controls, encryption, data retention, disaster recovery, or handling of sensitive audit data
The analyst-led model may create dependence on specialist judgment and continuity, although staffing and quality-control processes are not disclosed
business_risks: Potential concentration in services related to a small set of major software vendors, particularly Oracle
Vendor policy, audit-practice, licensing-model, or channel-program changes could affect demand and service economics
Oracle partnership and reseller activity may create perceived independence concerns despite the company's claim that it is wholly independent
Reliance on expert analysts may make growth dependent on recruiting and retaining scarce licensing expertise
Anonymized case studies and self-reported savings make outcome claims difficult to validate externally
The Miro Consulting/ECCO Select naming inconsistency may weaken brand clarity and customer confidence
The performance guarantee could create margin or dispute risk because detailed eligibility, measurement, and exclusion terms are not disclosed
marketing_message: The company positions itself as a proactive, expert-led software asset management provider that helps enterprises maximize software ROI, maintain compliance, reduce audit exposure, negotiate better terms, and control cloud and support costs—with a guarantee that identified savings will exceed its fees.
messaging_gaps: The relationship between Miro Consulting and ECCO Select is not explained
Claims such as 'leading,' 'only guaranteed,' 'original,' and 'most experienced' are not supported with comparative market evidence
The homepage vendor list differs from the services page: Adobe appears on the services page but not in the homepage hero, while detailed Adobe offerings are absent
AWS optimization is demonstrated in case studies but is not clearly defined in the main service catalog
The extent of current Salesforce and Adobe capabilities is not documented beyond high-level service references
The website does not clearly distinguish proprietary software capabilities from analyst processes and consulting methods
No roadmap, announced capabilities, or future product plans are provided
The performance guarantee lacks detailed terms, qualification rules, calculation methodology, and exclusions
